blocker.summary: r437 proved (hardware watchpoint) the null global pointer sub_821D6C20 crashes on (r436) is never written during the run; static search for its writer was attempted via Ghidra but returned zero hits because sub_821D6C20 was never disassembled in the queried project. r438 resized PinnedShaderRuntime's shared-memory SSBO to 512 MiB (verified, but deliberately not committed -- entangled with the r433-catalogued native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog) and fixed/committed a real, isolated build.py gap (missing ac6_native_guest_threads_tests target). r439 did two things. First, a comprehensive text search across all 77 XenonRecomp-generated ppc_recomp.*.cpp translation units (broader coverage than any single Ghidra project) for the literal offset 23960 (the only natural immediate encoding of guest address 0x82935D98) found the same zero-writer result -- only PPC_LOAD_U32 occurrences, all inside sub_821D6C20 itself. Second, and more importantly, r439 found r437's Ghidra methodology was flawed: the project it queried (ace-combat-6) points at game-files/default.xex, SHA acc302c1... -- a stale copy, DIFFERENT from the actually-qualified retail XEX (6eefba42..., verified identical across every codegen-*/assets/ directory in the real build tree) that every report in this chain investigates. The correct project is ac6-us (points at build/ntsc-uj/source/assets/default.xex, the right SHA). Both searches were rerun against ac6-us: identical zero-hit results, so r437's conclusion holds, verified this time against the right binary -- but the project-selection mistake is corrected for future cycles (use ac6-us, never ace-combat-6, for this chain). No new writer-finding avenue exists without either (1) writing/adapting a non-readonly disassembly-seeding script correctly SHA-gated to ac6-us/6eefba42 (the one such script that exists, SeedPdataExtentDisassembly.java, is gated to the wrong acc302c1 XEX and doesn't apply as-is), or (2) the native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438). Both remain open for r440, dependent on user direction rather than further autonomous investigation.
